summary: Current R-6 cab on a 10-ft timber tower, built 1959 as the fourth lookout on Red Mountain; a 2006 windstorm wrecked it and volunteers rebuilt it by 2010.

facts.design: R-6 wooden flat-top cab (15 by 15 ft) on a 10 ft timber tower; an example of the design that replaced the L-4 lookouts

staffing.status: not staffed; satellites now used for fire detection (WTA); Forest Service no longer uses it to spot fires (Willhite)

access.note: Vehicle road permanently gated at its junction with Forest Road 60; visitors walk in. No source says the cab interior is open to visitors or rentable yet.

visit.trail_note: Indian Racetrack Trail (#171) from a trailhead on Forest Road 65 beyond Falls Creek Horse Camp; about 3.4 miles to the gated FR 6048 road, then up to the tower base (WTA).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Mt. Adams Ranger District cooperator)

events.note: First structure on the summit, an 8x8 ft cedar cab (firelookout.com and WTA say 1910; Willhite and PCT Washington say 1913)
Cupola cabin replaced the first cab, about 1919
L-4 cab went up with a garage beside it (firelookout.com, Willhite)
PCT Washington dates the garage to 1938; firelookout.com and Willhite date it to 1935
Staffed 24 hours a day as an Aircraft Warning Station during World War II (NHLR gives 1942-43); garage converted to living quarters in 1942
Present 10 ft timber tower with R-6 cab; the fourth lookout on the site
December 2006 windstorm blew the roof and walls apart and damaged radio facilities for the county sheriff; PCT Washington dates it December 14
Matt Haldeman began a volunteer restoration; walls re-erected and a new roof installed for the winter
Passport in Time crew of 13 restored the lookout and garage; interior walls and flooring finished (PCT Washington dates volunteer labor to 2007-2008)

corrections.why: NHLR, firelookout.com and Willhite all describe a 10-ft timber tower (about 3.0 m); 4.0 m matches none of them

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and WTA give 1910 for the first cab; Willhite and PCT Washington give 1913. The story reports both; the 1910 event is kept with the disagreement noted.
firelookout.com and Willhite place the L-4 cab and garage in 1935; PCT Washington dates the garage to 1938. The story reports both.
PCT Washington gives December 14, 2006; firelookout.com says December 2006; WTA says the winter of 2006. The story reports the range.

resolved_conflicts.field: Passport in Time crew dates (2007-2008 vs 2010)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: PCT Washington describes Passport in Time volunteer labor in 2007 and 2008; Willhite and WTA describe a 13-person crew in 2010. Both are reported; all accounts agree the restoration was finished by 2010.
NHLR gives 4,911 ft (1,497 m), which matches the record's 1496.9 m; firelookout.com gives 4968 ft. No change proposed.

sources.title: Red Mountain Lookout via Indian Racetrack

notes_for_editor: Height: record 4.0 m is unsupported; sources give a 10-ft tower (proposed 3.0 m). The record's 1910 'built' event is the first cab; the present tower (1959) is added as its own event. Dates for the first cab (1910 vs 1913) and the restoration crews (2007-08 vs 2010) conflict; both are reported. Access is marked restricted because the road is gated and no source documents public entry to the cab. Rental is a plan in the sources (2010 quote, undated pages); recreation.gov and the Forest Service were not checked, so a human should confirm current rental and access status. All source pages are undated except the 2010 PCT quote. PCT Washington's 1913 first-cab date and 1938 garage date were added on this check. The WTA route is 3.1 miles plus 0.3 mile to the gated road (about 3.4 miles), and the story now ends that figure at the gate. No climbing advice is given.
